messages:
maria: follow-up from the RFC thread - i'm proposing we introduce an eviction-currency primitive to decouple eviction authority from fast-path residency. goal: reduce eviction thrash while letting routers prefer local hot copies.

jack: eviction-currency? curious, sketch it out. how is it different from leases/epochs we've discussed?

maria: short: Lease = canonical mutator authority (can apply hard-evict/reassign). EvictionCurrency = float token balance that represents how much eviction a node can spend on behalf of tenants for locality decisions. Residency stays advisory (residency=true/false + score).

lee: LGTm conceptually. how does currency get minted/reclaimed? sounds like another global counter.

maria: minted at ownership handoff and on periodic top-ups. reclaimed by background demote work and garbage-collection. currency is per-tenant-per-shard so it's bounded and observable.

carol: ops: what user-visible effects? if a node runs out of currency but holds the lease, can it still serve reads/writes?

maria: yes. Lease always trumps currency. Currency only gates "prefer-local" routing and soft-evict decisions that would drop a local copy for fairness reasons. If currency==0, router will failover to remote nodes with residency true.

jack: wire example pls (pseudo):

GET /kv/key?shard=42
resp: { v:..., lease: "L-900", residency: { hot: true, score: 0.83, epoch: 2025-11-01T12:00Z }, evict_currency: 12.5 }

router: prefer nodes with hot && evict_currency>threshold.

lee: how do we avoid oscillation where routers chase score and cause currency churn?

maria: two mechanisms: (1) residency_ttl and score smoothing (EWMA), (2) a damped replenish rate so currency can't spike immediately after reclaim. also demote cooldown windows.

carol: metrics/alerts? i'll need a short list to wire dashboards.

maria: initial telemetry set: 
- shard_residency_fraction (per-tenant shard gauge)
- mean_residency_score (histogram)
- evict_currency_balance (gauge)
- currency_replenish_rate (counter)
- remote_fetch_99p_latency (histogram)
- local_miss_ratio (derived)
guard rails for canary: remote_fetch_99p < baseline + 30ms, local_miss_ratio < 1.1x baseline, evict_currency_balance stdev stable.

jack: correctness question: during a lease transfer, what guarantees about reads/writes? if current owner demotes residency but keeps lease we could serve stale reads if we allowed some local-only mutations. need explicit rule.

maria: agreed. rule: while Lease held, node may serve reads and writes. Soft-demote only affects routing preference and indicates the node will not accept new pinned residency requests. Any demote -> transfer must do a Promote/HandOff RPC ack flow:

1) owner sets demote_start (read-only residency)
2) target node starts bulk prefill if needed
3) owner waits for handoff_ack or times out
4) owner revokes lease (via lease-revoke), transfer completes

reads during demote must be linearizable via write-through to the canonical store. no cached-write-only allowed.

lee: are we introducing new RPCs? Promote/Prefill/HandOff?

maria: yes minimal set: RequestPrefill(shard, target), HandOffAck(shard, lease_id), RevokeLease(shard, lease_id). Keep them small.

carol: rollout plan? i want stages and rollback criteria.

maria: staged plan:
- stage 0: telemetry only (emit evict_currency + residency_score), routers ignore. 2 weeks baseline.
- stage 1: router opt-in per-tenant: prefer residency when currency>threshold. start with internal tenants. 1-week canary per tenant. rollback if remote_fetch_99p > baseline+30ms or local_miss_ratio>1.1x.
- stage 2: enable soft-demote flows and handoff RPCs for small shard set. validate metrics and handoff success rate. rollback if handoff_fail_rate>0.5%.
- stage 3: gradual fleet enable, add eviction-budget enforcement.

jack: fairness: how to prevent a noisy tenant from draining currency across nodes? sounds like we need per-tenant credit caps and reclaim windows.

maria: yes - plan: PerTenantCap + global_shed_rate. high-volume tenants get smaller per-node caps; enterprise tenants can request higher caps via admin API. reclaim policy prioritizes fairness windows.

lee: admin API? pin/unpin residency?

maria: admin/pin residency(shard, tenant, duration) — sets residency=true and credits don't get consumed while pinned. also admin/topup_currency(tenant, amount). must be auditable.

carol: observability additions: add a flame graph for router decisions (why chosen node) and a small debug endpoint returning last N demote/promote events for a shard. helps debug canary.

deploy-bot: canary infra: cluster canary-7 ready, feature-flag residency-currency=true in test namespace.

canary-bot: scheduled run: 2025-11-05T09:00Z, 2-hour ramp, tenants: [internal-alpha, internal-beta].

maria: i'll open D12999 with proto and router change. pls add review tags: @jack, @lee, @carol. i'll include a short migration tool to backfill evict_currency for existing shards (initial grant = 5.0).

jack: one more edge: what if handoff RPCs fail repeatedly? we need exponential backoff + metric (handoff_fail_count) and fallback plan to force lease revoke after long timeout with operator approval.

maria: add operator-only revoke path with audit log. add rollback flag to re-enable previous behavior.

lee: reading this, i'm +1. will review D12999 and proto. pls include unit tests for currency math and demote state machine.

carol: i'll prepare dashboards and a runbook with clear rollback steps. also will add an SLA impact check for priority customers.

maria: summary of action items: D12999 proto + migration script (maria), router changes and unit tests (jack/lee), dashboards & runbook (carol), canary execution (ops). thanks everyone.

jack: nice work, looks pragmatic. :thumbsup:

lee: lgtm, tagging for review.

carol: adding alarm widgets now.

maria: will ping when PR is ready for review.
